dataset.name: UCI Online Retail (real UK online-retailer transactions)
dataset.licence_note: CC BY 4.0 per UCI (verify); see app/ml/data/DATA_LICENSE.md
dataset.limits: Real invoices, but NO payment failures and NO recovery outcomes: it cannot train or score the recovery model. Bundled file is a one-week sample; pass --path for the full data set.

amount_shape.reading: Shape comparison only (log-spread of invoice totals); levels differ by currency and market.

interpretation: The simulator's amount spread (log-sd 1.0) is close to the real invoice-total spread, so the log-normal amount assumption is reasonable in shape.

Under the worst case — every real attempt failing — the detector holds more windows than on synthetic benign data. Those are wholesale customers placing several invoices within minutes; treating a burst of failures from such a customer as worth a human look is defensible, but it does mean B2B-heavy merchants will see more holds.
Under realistic failure rates the hold rate is far lower, because a hold needs several failures inside one hour.
Neither number says anything about recall on real fraud: this data set has no fraud labels.
